gloss: written impressions; book report; review essay

definitions.gloss: written impressions; book report; review essay
definitions.explanation: A piece of writing in which one describes their personal impressions, thoughts, and feelings about something they read, watched, or experienced. A staple of Japanese school assignments.

examples.japanese: {感想文|かんそうぶん}を{書|か}く。
{夏休|なつやす}みの{宿題|しゅくだい}で{読書|どくしょ}{感想文|かんそうぶん}を{書|か}かされた。
examples.english: I was made to write a book report as summer homework.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}を{観|み}た{後|あと}、{感想文|かんそうぶん}を{四百字|よんひゃくじ}{詰|づ}め{原稿用紙|げんこうようし}{三枚|さんまい}にまとめた。
examples.english: After watching the movie, I wrote up my impressions on three sheets of 400-character manuscript paper.

notes:
Composed of {感想|かんそう} (impressions, thoughts) + {文|ぶん} (writing, text). This is one of the most common school writing assignments in Japan, particularly the {読書|どくしょ}{感想文|かんそうぶん} (book report) assigned during summer break.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読書|どくしょ}{感想文|かんそうぶん} — book report (the most common type)
- {感想文|かんそうぶん}を{書|か}く — to write a review/report
- {映画|えいが}の{感想文|かんそうぶん} — movie review essay
- {感想文|かんそうぶん}コンクール — book report contest

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {読書|どくしょ}{感想文|かんそうぶん} is a defining feature of Japanese school culture. Students from elementary through high school are assigned to read a book and write their personal impressions. Many students dread this assignment, and it has become a common topic in discussions about Japanese education.

RELATED WORDS:
- {感想|かんそう} — impressions, thoughts (spoken or written)
- {書評|しょひょう} — book review; more formal and analytical than {感想文|かんそうぶん}
- {作文|さくぶん} — essay, composition; broader term for any written assignment
